Hub C dominates at 1.17, and the tail node F, whose neighbors E and G it outranks, comes second at 0.71, ahead of B 0.60; A ends lowest at 0.10." width="100%"} DomiRank centrality quantifies node dominance in their neighborhoods. The competition parameter sigma (or alpha) provides a tunable trade-off between local and global topological information: `d𝚪ᵢ(t)/dt = σ(dᵢ - Σⱼ Aᵢⱼ 𝚪ⱼ(t)) - 𝚪ᵢ(t)` Where: - `𝚪ᵢ` is the dominance score for node `i` - `σ` is the competition parameter - `dᵢ` is the degree of node `i` - `A` is the adjacency matrix Unlike eigenvector-type centralities (where being connected to important nodes makes you important), DomiRank identifies nodes that dominate their local structure. Being close to a dominant node can suppress your own dominance in high-competition contexts. For `σ -> 0`: Converges to degree centrality (only local information) For large `σ`: Identifies globally dominant nodes DomiRank was introduced to study network fragility: removing nodes in decreasing order of DomiRank tends to dismantle a network faster than removing them by degree or betweenness. It is useful for: - choosing which nodes to protect (or attack) in robustness studies - finding hubs that control their neighborhood without competing with other hubs - contrasting "dominant" and "submissive" positions, since scores can go negative The scores are computed by integrating the dynamics above with a fixed time step of `0.1` from a uniform starting point until they settle. The process only settles when `σ` is below a critical value set by the most negative eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix, so by default `σ` is chosen automatically as a fraction `alpha=` of that critical value (found by bisection, which runs the solver repeatedly). If the solver does not settle within `max_iter=` steps, or starts to diverge, a `RuntimeWarning` is issued and the last values are returned. Edge weights are ignored; in directed graphs degrees and neighbors refer to outgoing edges. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [sigma]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Competition parameter. If `None` (default), automatically computed from smallest eigenvalue and alpha. Higher values increase global competition for dominance. Small values (e.g., `0.01`) give scores roughly proportional to degree; values above the critical level make the dynamics diverge and trigger a `RuntimeWarning`. [alpha]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.95]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Alpha parameter for auto-computing sigma (`sigma = alpha / |λ_min|`). Only used if sigma is `None`. Must be positive. Defaults to `0.95`, meaning `95%` of the critical competition level, which emphasizes global structure while keeping the solver stable. Lower it for a more local, degree-like ranking. [method]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["iterative"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Solution method. Currently only `"iterative"` (the default) is implemented; any other value raises a `ValueError`. [tol]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1e-05]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Convergence tolerance for the iterative solver. The solver stops once the summed absolute rate of change over all nodes falls below `tol * n * 0.1`, where `n` is the number of nodes. Defaults to `1e-5`. Must be positive. Smaller values give more precise scores at the cost of more iterations (and also tighten the bisection used to pick `sigma=` automatically). [max_iter]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1000]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum number of time steps for the iterative solver. Defaults to `1000`. The same limit applies to each trial run during the automatic search for `sigma=`. Must be at least `3 * patience`. If it is reached before convergence, a `RuntimeWarning` is issued. [patience]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[10]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of steps between convergence checks. Defaults to `10`. At each check the solver tests for convergence and stops early, flagging divergence, if the largest update has grown at three consecutive checks. Must satisfy `max_iter >= 3 * patience`. [max_depth]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[50]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum bisection steps for finding smallest eigenvalue (when auto-computing sigma). Defaults to `50`. Each step runs the iterative solver once, so lower values speed up the automatic choice of `sigma=` at the cost of a less precise critical value. Ignored when `sigma=` is given. [return_sigma]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, return (centrality_dict, sigma) tuple or (Graph, sigma) tuple instead of just dict or Graph. Useful for seeing which value was picked automatically, or for reusing it on a related graph. Defaults to `False`. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Column name used to store the scores in the node DataFrame. If `None` (default), the column is named `"domirank_centrality"`. An existing column with the same name is overwritten. Only used when `return_dict=` is `False`. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, return the scores as a dictionary and leave the node DataFrame untouched. If `False` (default), store the scores under `attr_name=` and return the graph for method chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[int, float] or tuple[dict[int, float], float] or Graph or tuple[Graph, float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True` and `return_sigma=` is `False`: dictionary mapping node IDs to dominance scores. If `return_dict=` is `True` and `return_sigma=` is `True`: tuple of (centrality dict, sigma value). If `return_dict=` is `False` and `return_sigma=` is `False`: returns self for method chaining. If `return_dict=` is `False` and `return_sigma=` is `True`: tuple of (self, sigma value). Nodes with positive scores are dominant; negative scores indicate submissive nodes. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `method=` is not `"iterative"`, `alpha=` <= `0`, `tol=` <= `0`, or `max_iter=` < `3 * patience`. ::: ## Warns {.doc-warns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [RuntimeWarning]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the iterative solver does not converge within `max_iter=` steps or diverges. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} DomiRank (Engsig, Tejedor, Moreno, et al., 2024) is a *competitive* centrality: rather than rewarding proximity to important neighbors as eigenvector-family metrics do, it rewards nodes that suppress their neighbors' scores. The continuous-time dynamics $\dot\Gamma_i = \sigma(d_i - \sum_j A_{ij}\Gamma_j) - \Gamma_i$ settle into a steady state where high-degree nodes surrounded by low-degree neighbors accumulate dominance, while nodes adjacent to already-dominant neighbors go into deficit (their scores drop below zero). The steady state is reached by explicit time stepping, with each step costing $O(E)$, so the method scales to large sparse networks. The `sigma=` parameter tunes the competition strength: as $\sigma \to 0$ the ranking degenerates to degree centrality, while large $\sigma$ surfaces the small set of globally dominant nodes. When `sigma=` is left unset, an internal bisection search picks $\sigma = \alpha / |\lambda_{\min}(A)|$, which is empirically near the sweet spot between local and global information. ## Examples {.doc-examples} The graph below has two hubs, H1 (with leaves a1, a2, a3) and H2 (with leaves b1, b2), connected through a middle node M. Leaving `sigma=` unset auto-tunes the competition parameter. Both hubs come out strongly dominant, while M, squeezed between two dominant neighbors, gets the most negative score: ::: {#6a55ec7e .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["H1", "a1", "a2", "a3", "H2", "b1", "b2", "M"]) .add_edges([("H1", "a1"), ("H1", "a2"), ("H1", "a3"), ("a1", "a2"), ("H2", "b1"), ("H2", "b2"), ("H1", "M"), ("M", "H2")]) ) scores = graph.domirank_centrality(return_dict=True) {graph.get_label_from_id(nid): round(s, 3) for nid, s in sorted(scores.items())} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {'H1': 2.261, 'a1': -0.076, 'a2': -0.076, 'a3': -0.515, 'H2': 1.871, 'b1': -0.356, 'b2': -0.356, 'M': -0.871} ``` ::: ::: Passing `return_sigma=True` alongside also returns the sigma value that was auto-selected: ::: {#4c7a3a9c .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} scores, sigma = graph.domirank_centrality(return_dict=True, return_sigma=True) round(sigma, 4) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 0.4084 ``` ::: ::: Setting `sigma=` by hand controls the amount of competition. With a very small value there is almost none and the scores simply track degree (H1 first, then H2, the leaves with one neighbor last); with a moderate value the ranking is still positive throughout but the hubs pull further ahead: ::: {#0f64f9a0 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} local = graph.domirank_centrality(sigma=0.01, return_dict=True) moderate = graph.domirank_centrality(sigma=0.2, return_dict=True) { graph.get_label_from_id(nid): (round(local[nid], 3), round(moderate[nid], 3)) for nid in sorted(local) } ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` {'H1': (0.039, 0.665), 'a1': (0.019, 0.222), 'a2': (0.019, 0.222), 'a3': (0.01, 0.067), 'H2': (0.03, 0.53), 'b1': (0.01, 0.094), 'b2': (0.01, 0.094), 'M': (0.019, 0.161)} ``` ::: :::
